title: Motion and colour-independence regression guards
description:
Objective: lock in the two spec section 11.1 guarantees that are currently true only by accident, so they cannot silently regress.

READ THIS FIRST — THIS GAP IS MUCH SMALLER THAN ITS NAME. It was opened as "prefers-reduced-motion is unimplemented". That was WRONG, and an adversarial refutation pass confirmed the correction. Measured on disk:
- board-layout.css:68 ALREADY has @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce), containing scroll-behavior:auto (line 70), animation:none (74) and transition:none (75).
- goals-board-ban.test.ts:147 ALREADY pins that block as source text.
- THERE IS NO MOTION TO SUPPRESS. Exhaustive inventory across apps/control-room and the control-room packages: @keyframes 0, transform 0, requestAnimationFrame 0, setTimeout/setInterval 0, spinner/fade/slide/easing/cubic-bezier/duration/opacity 0. Exactly one .css file exists (77 lines). It has one transition: declaration, value none, and one animation: declaration, value none — both inside the reduced-motion block, i.e. suppressing motion that does not exist. The three skeletons (cr.board.skeleton, cr.goals.skeleton, cr.health.skeleton) are empty divs with no CSS rule at all. The only declarations that move anything in a real browser are scroll-snap-type and scroll-snap-align, already neutralised by scroll-behavior:auto.
- All three cr.banner.* ids that exist are ALREADY live regions: disconnected (frame.tsx:132) and lag (frame.tsx:139) via role="status", invalidated (approval-detail-plan.tsx:187) via aria-live="polite". The three the spec names that lack one — circuitbreaker, revision, refusal — do not exist as components at all.

A worker who starts adding a useReducedMotion hook, transition-suppression CSS, or a motion token layer is building suppressors for motion that does not exist. A worker who tries to "add aria-live to the banners that lack it" will find nothing to fix and may invent placeholder banners — a stub carrying a real cr.banner.* id is exactly the dishonesty the frame already guards against for cr.graph.*. Confirm the zero counts yourself first.

THE REAL DELIVERABLE is two regression guards plus one tightening:
1. Pin the motion inventory at zero, so the reduced-motion guarantee cannot be quietly falsified by a future stylesheet.
2. Assert the non-chip half of section 11.1 bullet 1 ("no colour-only encoding anywhere") against real renders. Only the truth-chip fragment is covered today, by auditTruthClassMonochrome. The board's own overlays and indicators are not.
3. Tighten gating-keyboard.test.tsx:102, which currently accepts role "status" OR "alert" for cr.banner.disconnected, where section 11.1 line 687 says banners announce POLITELY.

Owned paths: apps/control-room/src/a11y/** (new test files only) and apps/control-room/src/shell/gating-keyboard.test.tsx.

Hard dependencies: Accessibility latency hardening (task-ab8c9489ab6446c384e977a3e1cc8063) must reach DONE first — it owns src/a11y/** and is WORKING.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test
definitionOfDone: A source-text test pins the motion inventory at zero across every .css and .tsx under apps/control-room/src: it asserts the scanned file set is NON-EMPTY first, then that no file contains @keyframes, no transition: or animation: declaration with a value other than none, and no scroll-behavior: smooth. It MUST NOT ban scroll-snap-type or scroll-snap-align — board-layout.css uses both legitimately for spec section 4.16 column behavior, and banning them would fight the narrow-mode tasks.

The same test asserts every .css file under apps/control-room/src contains a @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block, and pins the existing block's contents (animation: none, transition: none, scroll-behavior: auto) so it cannot be deleted or hollowed out silently.

The non-chip half of section 11.1 bullet 1 is asserted against REAL rendered surfaces, not fragments: every rendered board card overlay, badge and indicator conveys its meaning in text or glyph and not by colour alone. Assert the swept element count is greater than zero before asserting zero violations, and report each violation with a stable reason code naming the offending test id.

gating-keyboard.test.tsx no longer accepts role="alert" for cr.banner.disconnected: each of the three existing banner ids is asserted to resolve to a POLITE live region (role="status" or aria-live="polite", never assertive/alert), per section 11.1 line 687.

Recorded as explicit not-applicable WITH the reason, never as a passing assertion over zero cases: (a) WCAG AA contrast — no colour value exists anywhere to measure. TruthSemanticTone is a prose union ("neutral slate", "amber"), the one stylesheet uses only the system keywords canvas and highlight, and there are zero hex/rgb/hsl/oklch literals in the app or any package. This needs a colour-token layer and is a separate task whose DoD cannot be written until tones resolve to values. (b) The graph half of bullet 1 (edges use pattern + arrowheads, critical path uses weight + pattern) — no graph surface exists; note that criticalPath already renders as a text SuppliedFact via board-card.tsx:43, so it is not colour-only today. (c) cr.banner.circuitbreaker, cr.banner.revision and cr.graph.refusal — those components do not exist, and no placeholder may be created to satisfy a sweep.

pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test passes, and each new guard is verified by mutating the production surface — add a transition to the stylesheet, and strip a badge's text label — confirming each guard goes red, then reverting.
taskRails: Pinned UI spec: D:/projexts/moes/docs/plans/2026-08-05-moe-v1-control-room-spec.md SHA-256 C55AF8A9FC7386E6492FD57E34A4B8321ABAAE4E4E08FF38703544B58B0BEF1F. Section 11.1 is lines 681-687.

Do NOT add production code to satisfy this task. Its own measurement is that zero production changes are required: the reduced-motion block exists, there is no motion to suppress, and every banner that exists is already a live region. If you find yourself writing a hook or a stylesheet, re-read the description and confirm the zero counts before proceeding.

NEVER create a component just to give a sweep something to find. cr.banner.circuitbreaker, cr.banner.revision and cr.graph.refusal do not exist. A stub carrying a real cr.banner.* id would be a fabricated surface — exactly what the frame already refuses to do for cr.graph.*.

Do not reimplement auditLiveRegions, auditTruthClassMonochrome or any other predicate in apps/control-room/src/a11y/surface-audit.ts — consume them. Locate symbols by NAME, never by line number: that file is actively changing and every line number recorded here will be stale.

jsdom 30.0.1 implements neither window.matchMedia nor media-query evaluation, and document.styleSheets.length is 0 because Vitest stubs the CSS import. No assertion may be driven by an actual prefers-reduced-motion match. The motion guard is a source-text pin and must be labelled as one.
Do not assert a global test COUNT as a completion signal. This is a shared worktree with other agents adding tests; a total-count assertion is not a property of this task and will drift.
Keep each file below 400 lines, target 250. Explicit owned paths only; no git add -A.

implementationPlan.description:
DoD 1 + 2 — create the motion guard as a SOURCE-TEXT PIN (taskRail 5: jsdom 30 has no matchMedia and document.styleSheets.length is 0, so no assertion may be driven by a real media-query match; label the file as a source-text pin in a header comment).

Discover .css files by walking apps/control-room/src with node:fs readdirSync recursive, resolved from fileURLToPath(import.meta.url) — NOT a hand-written file list, which rots as stylesheets are added. Guard against the scan root narrowing: assert the discovered set contains the six named stylesheets (responsive, control-room, chrome, shell, surfaces, shell-layout) AND that the count is >= 13.

Assert, in this order:
1. Discovered .css set is NON-EMPTY and contains those six names.
2. The motion sweep found a NON-ZERO number of motion declarations (epic rail 6 — a sweep matching nothing must not pass). Count declarations matching /@keyframes|(^|[;{\s])(transition|animation)\s*:/ whose value is not `none`; assert >= 5.
3. styles/responsive.css contains '@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)', a universal selector matching /\*,\s*\*::before,\s*\*::after/u, and ALL FOUR neutralising declarations verbatim: 'animation-duration: 0.01ms !important', 'animation-iteration-count: 1 !important', 'transition-duration: 0.01ms !important', 'scroll-behavior: auto !important'.
4. The reset is actually LOADED, not dead code: styles/control-room.css contains '@import "./responsive.css"'.
5. No stylesheet anywhere contains 'scroll-behavior: smooth'.
6. Pin the three EXISTING same-file blocks so they cannot be hollowed out: board/board-layout.css:68 block still contains 'scroll-behavior: auto', 'animation: none', 'transition: none'; same for approvals/approval-layout.css and shell/shell-layout.css.

MUST NOT ban scroll-snap-type or scroll-snap-align — board-layout.css uses both for spec section 4.16 and banning them fights the narrow-mode tasks. MUST NOT ban motion outright: the governor's note is explicit that a diff satisfying this by BANNING motion is a rejection. The property is that motion is GATED, not absent.
implementationPlan.note:
Created a11y/motion-inventory.test.ts as a labelled SOURCE-TEXT PIN (taskRail 5 header comment explains why: jsdom 30 has no matchMedia and document.styleSheets.length is 0). 8 tests, all green.

Arms, in the plan's order:
1. Scan root not narrowed: basename(SRC_ROOT) === "src", discovered .css count >= 13, and all six named stylesheets present. Three independent detectors for a hop-count root that silently shrinks.
2. NON-ZERO before anything: total motion declarations >= 5 AND motion-bearing file set non-empty. Everything downstream is vacuous without this.
3. THE LOAD-BEARING ARM, stronger than the plan asked for. Rather than only asserting responsive.css exists, it asserts per motion-bearing stylesheet: it either contains its own @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block OR is @imported into styles/control-room.css (which loads the universal !important reset). Violations are frozen { code: "MOTION_WITHOUT_REDUCED_MOTION_GATE", stylesheet } so the failure names the offending sheet. This generalises: a NEW stylesheet that carries motion, is loaded component-side, and has no block of its own goes RED. Motion is proven GATED, never banned.
4. Global reset pinned: block extracted by brace matching, must match /\*,\s*\*::before,\s*\*::after/u and contain all four declarations verbatim.
5. Reset proven LOADED not dead code: control-room.css contains '@import "./responsive.css"'.

Same-file blocks pinned PER FILE at their actual contents — board-layout.css 3 declarations, shell-layout.css 3, approval-layout.css 2 (no scroll-behavior; the file's own comment says "Motion only: animation and transition. implementationPlan.description:
DoD 1, JS half — extend motion-inventory.test.ts to ban JS-driven motion, which the CSS global reset provably CANNOT neutralise (a reset on animation-duration/transition-duration does not reach requestAnimationFrame loops or Web Animations API calls). This is the arm that makes the guard load-bearing rather than decorative.

Sweep .ts/.tsx under apps/control-room/src EXCLUDING *.test.* and *fixtures*, and assert ZERO matches for: requestAnimationFrame, .animate(, 'framer-motion', 'react-spring'.

DO NOT ban setTimeout or setInterval. Measured: live/live-board-feed.ts:98 and live/live-event-feed.ts:100 both use setTimeout, and they are feed reconnect/poll BACKOFF timers, not animation. A blanket timer ban would go red on correct production code and would have to be weakened — the exact guard-rot failure epic rail 6 exists to prevent. Record that exclusion and its reason in a comment.

Assert the scanned .ts/.tsx file set is NON-EMPTY before asserting zero matches, so a broken scan root cannot pass as a clean sweep.
implementationPlan.note:
Added the JS-motion half to motion-inventory.test.ts. 10 tests green (was 8).

New arm "bans JS-driven motion, which no stylesheet reset can neutralise": sweeps .ts/.tsx under src excluding *.test.* and *fixtures*, asserts the scanned set is >= 40 files BEFORE asserting zero matches (63 production sources measured today, so the floor catches a broken scan root without going red on normal churn). Zero matches for requestAnimationFrame, .animate(, framer-motion, react-spring. Violations are frozen { code: "JS_DRIVEN_MOTION", source, token } so a failure names both the file and which token it tripped.

Why this arm is the load-bearing one, recorded in a header comment: the global CSS reset overrides animation-duration and transition-duration, which provably cannot reach a requestAnimationFrame loop or a Web Animations element.animate() call. So JS motion must be ABSENT where CSS motion is merely GATED — the two halves assert different properties for a stated reason.

setTimeout/setInterval NOT banned, verified on disk first: live/live-board-feed.ts:98 and live/live-event-feed.ts:100 both use setTimeout for feed reconnect/poll backoff (live-event-feed.ts:34 even documents it as injectable, "production uses setTimeout"). Banning timers would go red on correct production code. Exclusion and reason recorded in the comment above JS_MOTION_TOKENS.

Second new arm "keeps backoff timers legal so the JS ban cannot rot into a weakened guard": positively asserts both setTimeout call sites still exist AND that the ban list contains neither setTimeout nor setInterval. This makes the exclusion a tested decision rather than a comment someone can quietly reverse — if a future agent widens the ban to timers, this arm fails instead of the widening shipping and then being weakened back.

Tests/fixtures are excluded from the sweep because they must name the banned tokens in order to ban them; that exclusion is stated in the helper's doc comment.

implementationPlan.description:

Report each violation as a frozen { code, testId } object mirroring the AuditViolation shape in surface-audit.ts, with the stable code 'INDICATOR_COLOUR_ONLY', and assert on the full violation array so the failure message names the offending test id.

implementationPlan.note:
Created a11y/colour-independence.test.tsx. 18 tests green (15 per-surface + 3). 225 lines.

Follows ui-wide-acceptance.test.tsx exactly: CORE_SURFACE_FIXTURES + OPS_SURFACE_FIXTURES (15 surfaces), each mounted through the real ShellFrame with the LAGGING affordance, IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT in beforeAll, cleanup in afterEach. Symbols imported by NAME with .js extensions; no barrel.

Sweep: [data-testid^='cr.board.'], [data-testid^='cr.fact.'], [data-testid^='cr.chip.']. Per-element predicate:
- cr.fact.* -> cr.label AND cr.value must each have non-empty text, read SEPARATELY. The wrapper's own textContent would hide a blanked label behind its siblings' text, which is exactly the step-7 mutation drill, so that shortcut is not taken.
- cr.chip.* -> non-empty accessible name AND non-empty cr.glyph or cr.shortlabel.
- everything else -> non-empty text or accessible name.
Violations are frozen { code: "INDICATOR_COLOUR_ONLY", testId }, mirroring the AuditViolation shape, asserted as a whole array so the failure names the offending id. Swept count asserted > 0 BEFORE zero-violations on every surface (epic rail 6). No global test-count assertion (taskRail 6).

TWO REAL FINDINGS from the first red run, both fixed in the guard rather than papered over:
1. cr.board.filter.terminated (checkbox) and cr.board.columnjump (select) were reported as violations. FALSE POSITIVE: board-surface.tsx:199/207 names them with <label for>, not aria-label. Added accessibleName() resolving aria-label, title, aria-labelledby, label[for=id] and an ancestor <label>. Reading only aria-label would have reported two correctly-labelled controls as colour-only.
2. cr.board.joinstrip was reported. FALSE POSITIVE: it is an empty aria-live container until a join arrives. Added encodesSomething(): an element with no text, no element children, that is not a form control and has no role/data-tone/data-truth-class renders NOTHING and so cannot encode anything by colour. Deliberately narrow — anything with a tone attribute a stylesheet could colour, or any control, still must carry text.

GAP FOUND AND CLOSED — this is the DoD 3 gap itself. ui-wide-core-fixtures.tsx:144 builds the board with cards={[]}, so EVERY board card overlay is outside the shared fixture sweep; the fixture-driven arm can never see them. I cannot edit that file (owned paths are NEW a11y test files only), so the new arm "covers the board's own card overlays, which the shared fixture never renders" mounts the production BoardSurface directly with a real BoardCardProjection and a real BoardJoinSummary, then asserts all five section 11.1 overlays are present in the swept set by name (criticalpath, disposition, held, qualification, suspect) and that the audit is clean. Real production component, real render, no mock.

Truth-chip half CONSUMED not reimplemented (taskRail 4): auditTruthClassMonochrome() from ./surface-audit.js asserted to equal { checked: 5, violations: [] }.

Self-caught defect: I first wrote expect(result.checked).toBeGreaterThan(swept.length - 1), which is checked > checked-1 — tautologically true and therefore vacuous. Replaced with toBeGreaterThan(BOARD_OVERLAYS.length).

implementationPlan.note:
DoD 4 done. 21 tests green across the two files; package typecheck clean.

gating-keyboard.test.tsx — the tightening the DoD names. Line 102 was `expect(["status", "alert"]).toContain(banner.getAttribute("role"))`, which accepted an assertive interruption. Replaced with a politeness() helper that returns a STABLE REASON CODE rather than a boolean: "ASSERTIVE" when role=alert or aria-live=assertive, "POLITE" when role=status or aria-live=polite, "NO_LIVE_REGION" otherwise — asserted as toBe("POLITE"). A boolean assertion would have failed with "expected false to be true"; this one says which way the banner stopped being polite. Assertive spellings are rejected BY NAME, so the guard cannot be satisfied by merely allowing the polite ones.
Also tightened cr.banner.lag in the same file (line ~130), which renders in that file's own LAGGING test. Both banners reachable from gating-keyboard's own render are now covered there, per the plan.
